summary.headline: Wakefit FY26 revenue rose 17% to INR1,489 crore, but Q4 revenue growth slowed to 13.5% and margins face near-term pressure from raw-material inflation.
summary.overview: Wakefit reported record FY26 revenue of INR1,489 crore (+17% YoY) with gross margin of 55.8% and reported EBITDA (ex other income) of INR182 crore (12.2%). Q4 revenue was INR344 crore (+13.5% YoY) with Q4 operating EBITDA at 6.3%, reflecting higher A&P spend and sharp raw-material inflation (polyol, TDI) from February onward. Management took two price increases of about 7-8% each (March and April), said April 2026 growth was better than JFM, and guided to no material margin change in Q1 FY27 versus March exit levels. It also outlined an 80+ net store addition plan for FY27 and a Jumbo store in early FY28.

segments.name: Retail (COCO and channel mix)
segments.commentary: Retail revenue grew 49% YoY in FY26; own channels (website plus COCO) were 67.2% of FY26 sales and more than 74% of Q4 sales. 139 COCO stores across 76 cities (about 4 lakh sq ft); 42 gross additions and about 8 closures in FY26.

guidance_outlook: FY27 aspiration: at least about 20% company-level revenue growth; management said it will do its best but declined to give formal guidance.
Near term: no material change or dilution in margin structure expected in Q1 FY27 versus March exit gross margin; gross margin expected to hold steady for April-June.
If price pressure persists, EBITDA could be hit by 1-2 percentage points while still chasing 20%+ growth, with market share protection prioritised.
Store plan: more than 80 net COCO additions in FY27 (regular formats of 600 to 5,500 sq ft); detailed specifics promised at Q1 results.
Capex for FY27 estimated at INR120-140 crore, mostly retail (Jumbo store, about 80 stores), not manufacturing capacity.
A&P spend expected to rise to about 7-8% of sales over the medium term (Q4 FY26 about 7.3%; FY26 about 5.7%).
ESOP expense for FY27 expected at about INR12 crore (FY26: INR33 million). Jumbo store (100,000+ sq ft) expected to open early FY28, with breakeven targeted in about 18-24 months.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex estimated at INR120-140 crore, primarily retail: Jumbo store (about 60-70% of its initial capex expected in FY27) and about 80 regular store openings.

Store count 139 COCO at FY26 end; about 40 gross new stores added in FY26 (management said 42 gross additions and about 8 closures); FY27 target is more than 80 net additions, with average store size shrinking so the additions count is slightly less than double the prior year's space.
Two Jumbo stores planned in FY28 (first around April-May 2027, second later in the year), outside the 80-store plan.
Manufacturing is in-house with no added capacity planned; management said adjacent categories will be sourced as white label or trade to avoid capex.
demand_pricing: Two price increases of about 7-8% each in March and April 2026 (roughly 15% cumulative); management said the industry took similar increases, leaving brand-to-brand consumer price gaps within 1-3%.

Raw-material procurement inflation of 25-30% on some inputs, 15-20% on others, and 5-6% on the rest; overall mattress COGS basket up about 10% on current procurement, and about 30% if crude stays near $100 and old stock runs out.
April 2026 growth was said to be better than January-March, but management reserved comment until Q1 results; some volume slowdown is expected short term, offset by higher ASP.
Competition has intensified over the last 6-9 months from INR100-300 crore revenue players with lower cost structures, with higher ad spend and price matching.
Management said organized brands with in-house manufacturing could gain share from unorganised, contract-made foam during supply disruption; it did not quantify this.

Repeat revenue and cross-category sales are the two KPIs tracked monthly; volume growth is not a KPI and was not disclosed. Returns under the 100-day trial policy are below double digits as a share of sales.

qa_highlights.question: What inflation is the mattress COGS basket facing, and can the EBITDA margin hold for FY27 if crude stays near $100?
qa_highlights.answer: Current procurement inflation is about 10%, versus about 30% if spot prices persist after old stock runs out. Management said EBITDA could fall 1-2 percentage points while it chases 20%+ growth.

qa_highlights.question: How big are the adjacent categories, and what is the right to win?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described the expansion as completing the portfolio (live plants, décor, fertilizers) through white-label and trade sourcing with no capex, mainly for the Jumbo store. It gave no revenue or share targets.

qa_highlights.question: Has COCO expansion slowed (137 to 139 stores in Q4), and what is the FY27 plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it paused in December to recalibrate and promised more than 80 net additions in FY27, with specifics at Q1 results. Parul Gupta said about 40 stores were added in FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Will the rising own-channel mix (about 75%) hurt margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said COCO stores hold only display inventory, so no margin drag is expected. It also said own channels avoid third-party commissions, and it will keep marketplaces and MBOs as partners.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the rent outgo, ROU decline, and non-operating income.
qa_highlights.answer: Rent was about INR20 crore in Q4 and INR80 crore in FY26. The ROU asset fell because fewer new leases were added than planned. Non-operating items (about INR40 crore in Q4 and INR63 crore in FY26) are mainly unrealised MTM gains on mutual funds and FX.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up the INR958 crore investable cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Pre-IPO cash was about INR417-450 crore, IPO net proceeds about INR377-400 crore, and only INR4.5 crore of IPO money has been used. The rest is internal accrual. Other financial assets rose to INR356 crore on fixed deposits with 3-12 month maturities.

risks_watch: Raw-material inflation (polyol, TDI, plywood, MDF) tied to crude and the Middle East conflict; management said the margin hit could be 1-2 percentage points if prices stay high.
Q1 FY27 volume response to the roughly 15% cumulative price increase; management said volume growth is not a tracked KPI.
Deferred tax charge of INR98 crore in Q4 FY26 and its effect on reported PAT; deferred tax reversals or charges could recur.
Execution risk on more than 80 net store additions in FY27 and the Jumbo store breakeven target of 18-24 months.
Rising A&P spend (toward 7-8% of sales) and intensifying competition from low-cost players, which could pressure operating EBITDA.
Q1 FY27 results (store plan specifics, April-May growth) are the next checkpoint.
Unrealised MTM and FX gains that sit in non-operating income and may distort reported profit.
summary.management_tone: Confident on brand, store and market-share strategy and on April trading, but cautious on margins and volumes in the near term. Management avoided formal guidance, deferred store-plan detail and volume figures to Q1, and was candid that competition and inflation pose risks.
key_quotes: We are very, very protective of our market share on all channels because that acquisition of market share has a compounding effect.
So in about 18 months or so, we should aspire to breakeven.
April definitely has been way better than JFM.
We don't have a habit of providing guidance, especially in a normal behavior time itself, we worry about how to provide something that is sustainable and achievable.
